items.stem: A Section migration throws 'Unable to resolve reference identifier (Property: StaffId; Source System ID: 0017738)'. What's the typical root cause?

options.text: The referenced entity's source system isn't listed in its [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers], so that source id has no mapping

items.explanation: The child referenced a Staff by a source id the engine couldn't map — because Staff hadn't registered that source system. Add it to the entity's [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers].

misconceptions.b: The engine resolved most ids fine; this is a per-entity mapping gap, not an outage.

items.stem: A run throws 'SqlException: Violation of UNIQUE KEY constraint ... Cannot insert duplicate key'. What does this usually mean?

options.text: The engine tried to Create a record that already exists because StarBridge had no mapping linking it (so it didn't Update)
Two runs executed at the same time
The POCO has a non-nullable property

items.explanation: No StarBridge mapping meant the engine treated an existing record as new and tried to Insert it. The fix is to establish the mapping (or let [DuplicationKey] dedup match it) so it Updates instead.

misconceptions.c: The nullable rule causes change-detection problems, not a UNIQUE KEY insert violation.

items.stem: 'System.InvalidOperationException: No sink exists for the X entity type' points to a problem with:

options.text: Connector wiring/discovery — the [Sink] for X is missing, mis-typed, or not discoverable by MEF
A network timeout to the destination

items.explanation: MEF couldn't bind a sink for X — usually a missing/incorrect [Sink(DestinationSystem=...)] attribute (or a duplicate/ambiguous one). Check the connector's wiring (L2.5).

misconceptions.b: Empty source data wouldn't say 'no sink exists' — that's about discoverability of the connector.

items.stem: A run throws 'No sink exists for the Course entity type', yet CourseSink compiles fine. What's wrong, and how do you fix it?
rubric: It compiles but MEF didn't discover/bind a sink for Course
Cause: the [Sink(DestinationSystem = typeof(...))] attribute is missing, wrong, or duplicated/ambiguous so MEF can't bind exactly one
Fix: ensure exactly one correctly-attributed ISink<Course> so MEF discovers it
items.sampleAnswer: Compiling isn't the same as being discovered: Synnduit finds connectors via MEF attributes, not by type. 'No sink exists for Course' means MEF couldn't bind one — almost always the [Sink(DestinationSystem = typeof(...))] attribute is missing or wrong on CourseSink (or there are two and it's ambiguous). Fix the attribute so there's exactly one discoverable ISink<Course>.

items.stem: Describe your loop for resolving an unfamiliar Synnduit exception.
rubric: Get the exact message text (console, or EntityException / Operation-Message in StarBridge)
Search ExceptionHistoryWithResolutions/ for that error — most are already documented
Trace to the root cause and apply the documented fix (and add a new entry if it's novel)
items.sampleAnswer: First get the exact message — from the console or from StarBridge (the Operation/Message text). Then search the ExceptionHistoryWithResolutions/ folder for that error; most production exceptions are already there with a root cause and fix. Apply the documented fix, and if it's a new one, add it to the folder.
